audit_findings.title: The valuation date is after its own Pizza Hut completion triggers, but the DCF still values the pre-sale perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.3 billion expected net proceeds, plus a contingent $75 million earn-out; Pizza Hut generated $340 million of 2025 operating profit and $135 million in first-half 2026; held-for-sale assets less liabilities were $468 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor OE includes Pizza Hut earnings, while a post-sale bridge should remove those earnings and related obligations, add net proceeds, and include retained costs and transition-service economics.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently intend to complete this strategic options review in 2026, and there can be no assurance this review will result in any specific outcome or transaction.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation date follows the stated August 7 and September 1 completion triggers, yet the latest filed balance sheet is pre-closing. This is a demonstrated timing and perimeter mismatch if the reported completions occurred. The direction is mixed because losing Pizza Hut earnings reduces value while receiving proceeds increases it. Expected proceeds alone equal about 10.5% of the $21.995 billion base equity value, so the issue is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the completion filings and definitive closing statements, then rerun the valuation using retained-YUM OE and a post-closing bridge including actual net proceeds, taxes, retained liabilities, stranded overhead, transition-service income and any earn-out treatment.

audit_findings.title: A multibillion-dollar unreserved IRS claim sits ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.818 billion filed exposure: $2.1 billion tax, $418 million penalties and $2.3 billion accrued interest; equal to $17.21 per diluted share and 21.9% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any payment is a cash claim ahead of common equity and would reduce the equity bridge; related recurring interest or financing costs could also reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The IRS asserts an underpayment of tax of approximately $2.1 billion plus $418 million in penalties for fiscal year 2014.
audit_findings.explanation: The asserted exposure is demonstrated, but liability and settlement probability remain unresolved because YUM disputes the claim and records no reserve. Full exposure materially exceeds the $699 million cash bridge addition and is large relative to every scenario value, making probability-weighted treatment necessary.
audit_findings.action: Update the Tax Court record, obtain tax-counsel probability ranges and identify indemnities, tax assets or insurance offsets; rerun the bridge under probability-weighted settlement amounts including updated interest.

audit_findings.title: Franchise incentives may be recurring reinvestment omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed franchise-incentive assets were $209 million at December 31, 2025 and $172 million at June 30, 2026 outside the held-for-sale presentation; recurring cash additions are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring cash incentives needed to produce unit or same-store growth should reduce OE or be linked explicitly to the growth scenarios; subsequent amortization as reduced revenue does not capture the original cash timing.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, from time-to-time we provide consideration to franchisees in the form of cash (e.g. cash payments to offset new build costs) or other incentives (e.g. free or subsidized equipment) with the intent to drive new unit development or same-store sales growth that will result in higher future revenues for the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that YUM funds franchise incentives and capitalizes them, but it does not supply the annual cash-additions reconciliation needed to determine what was omitted from OE. The balance movements cannot establish cash spending because they combine additions, amortization, impairments and held-for-sale transfers. Value could be overstated, but materiality is unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile annual cash additions by brand to amortization, impairments, disposals and held-for-sale transfers; identify amounts already captured in OE or capex and rerun each growth scenario with its recurring incentive requirement.

audit_findings.title: Equity-settled deferred compensation may be missing from the share denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncounted EID phantom shares would increase fully diluted shares and reduce value per share without changing aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Deferrals into the phantom shares of our Common Stock will be distributed in shares of our Common Stock, under the LTIP, at a date as elected by the employee and therefore are classified in Common Stock on our Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that some EID balances must ultimately be distributed in common shares, but it does not disclose the outstanding phantom-share balance or trace it into the supplied 279.974085 million diluted-share denominator. Omission is therefore a possibility rather than a demonstrated denominator error, and its materiality cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the EID phantom-common-share balance at the valuation date and reconcile it award by award to the cover count, options/SARs, RSUs/PSUs and every other component of the diluted-share calculation; rerun per-share values for any net omitted shares.

audit_findings.title: The underfunded U.S. pension obligation is a senior non-debt claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $104 million funded shortfall, equal to $0.37 per diluted share and 0.47% of the $21.995 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any portion of accumulated pension underfunding not captured by normalized OE would be deducted from the equity bridge or reflected through future deficit-funding cash costs.
audit_findings.evidence: Our two most significant plans are in the U.S. and combined had a projected benefit obligation (“PBO”) of $774 million and a fair value of plan assets of $670 million at December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The $104 million shortfall is demonstrated and senior to common equity, although the incremental adjustment may be smaller because pension costs and contributions already pass through reported cash flows. Even deducting the entire filed shortfall would reduce base value from $78.56 to about $78.19 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 2026 funded status and expected mandatory contributions, and verify what normalized OE already captures; adjust only for an incremental amount not represented in forecast cash costs.

audit_findings.title: Lease guarantees create contingent claims not represented by lease expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $300 million undiscounted maximum and $250 million present value at June 30, 2026; the present value equals $0.89 per diluted share and 1.14% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Expected guarantee payments upon franchisee default, net of recoveries and any recorded guarantee liability, would reduce OE or the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the potential amount of undiscounted payments we could be required to make in the event of non-payment by the primary lessee was approximately $325 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The contingent exposure exists, but the filing says the recorded expected-loss liability is not material and cross-default rights reduce expected loss. Even deducting the entire $250 million present-value ceiling would lower base value only from $78.56 to about $77.67 per share, far too little to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Update which guarantees were transferred or retained in the Pizza Hut sales and monitor concentrated franchisee distress; rerun only if expected payments net of recoveries become materially larger than the currently recorded exposure.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings

audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2021 $30.0m (18.3% of filed D&A); FY2025 $26.0m (12.6% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: No overstatement is present because the unidentified amount remains expensed. Even the conservative sensitivity that treats the entire FY2025 residual as a recurring eligible add-back leaves all scenario values far below the $150.71 market price and does not alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A from filed asset schedules and rerun the historical OE trend only for components demonstrated to be eligible add-backs; retain the expense treatment for anything still unidentified.
